{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjqe88AAAABZEYNKg", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3INzhCqqe4", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3IN", "number": 49, "title": "Make AI regulars fully autonomous after setup and remove manual post-generation controls from the normal experience", "body": "## Problem

PC-VAN is meant to feel like a living text-based community of ten fictional regulars. A visitor should read the boards, write messages and receive natural later responses without directing the AI. The app already has independent resident scheduling (#35), initial conversations (#37) and explicit local-model setup (#39/#47), **but its normal AI Settings still exposes a manual post-production workflow**: choose persona/forum/reply, press `投稿案を生成` / `GENERATE`, inspect `PREVIEW`, then `SEND` or `DISCARD`. The README and in-terminal legacy `SETTINGS → 3` menu advertise these steps.

This suggests users must tell the residents what to post and when. That is the wrong mental model. Manual generation is a **developer/diagnostic mechanism**, not a normal part of joining PC-VAN.

**Product intent:** after one-time, clearly consented model setup, the ten residents independently participate according to their individual schedules, interests, conversations and relationships. The human user never needs to generate or approve their posts.

## Expected outcome

- **Ordinary user flow:** initial bundled thirty posts are readable immediately. The app's `設定 / Options → AIモデル・活動` offers a neutral model setup action, explicit download consent, overall activity/pause and per-resident lifestyle preferences. Once the model is prepared, the user simply browses, writes and replies *inside the terminal*. Resident posts/replies are automatically generated and saved when due, including delayed responses to both the human and other regulars.
- **No manual post-generation UX in the normal product:** remove `投稿案を生成`, manual persona/board/reply target selection, `投稿案を表示`, `投稿案を保存`, `投稿案を破棄` and the visible `GENERATE / PREVIEW / SEND / DISCARD` menu from ordinary Settings and Help. Keep individual resident **profile editing** because it configures their behavior; that is not the same as instructing a resident to post. If a developer really needs an explicit one-shot generator, make it strictly an intentionally opened advanced/test-only tool, with no default invitation or expectation that visitors use it; removing it altogether is acceptable.
- **Actual automatic operation is mandatory:** do not merely hide buttons. Confirm that the scheduler alone, with stored model authorization, selects independent resident actions and invokes WebLLM, validates them and commits posts. No manually reviewed draft, `GENERATE` call, open Settings dialog, `RECONNECT` command or user submit action is needed to make automatic work progress when due.
- **Immersive normal UX:** the terminal shows ordinary period-style author handles, titles, replies and dates. Technical AI diagnostics, artificial-author provenance and errors stay in on-demand Settings → Details/About. A small neutral AI-model status is fine; avoid implying real remote participants or emphasizing “ten AI people” in ordinary screens.

### Timing & technical boundaries

- Keep the existing per-resident life/routine-based scheduling and genuine quiet periods. **Do not generate an immediate canned reply to every post**, promise a new post immediately on first model load, rotate ten names at a fixed global rate, or simulate an always-online remote service.
- While the page is visible and connected, due work is processed automatically; background work must not steal input focus, interrupt terminal composition or make the transcript unusable. On reopening, a bounded chronological catch-up is performed; no inference happens while the browser is closed.
- Preserve first-use explicit authorization before fetching hundreds of MB–GB of model assets. New worlds default to auto-activity enabled with conservative generation limits, **but** the app must never download substantial model data without affirmative consent. After consent, subsequent scheduled work should load/reuse the approved local model automatically when needed. A previously paused global/individual setting stays paused.
- Keep one WebLLM worker/model, serialization/cross-tab locking, bounded attempts and elapsed-time catch-up, idempotent storage and safe cancellation/retry handling. Preserve model/consent changes, restore/reset semantics and JSON provenance.

## Context

Inspect current `main` and instructions before implementation:

- `src/settings-dialog.ts`: **手動生成・投稿案の確認** subsection currently contains `.generate-ai`, `.preview-ai`, `.save-ai`, `.discard-ai`, and persona/forum/reply selectors. The settings dialog is correct for **modern AI setup and profile/activity preferences** (#47); the manual-generation controls are what should disappear from normal use.
- `src/commands.ts` and `src/settings.ts`: optional legacy typed `SETTINGS → 3` currently advertises `PERSONA`, `FORUM`, `REPLY`, `GENERATE`, `PREVIEW`, `SEND`, `DISCARD`. These are developer-oriented AI operations, not actual PC-VAN terminal activity; remove them from normal help and menus. Preserve **human** `WRITE`, `REPLY n`, handle registration and the terminal-only post composer introduced in #45.
- `src/ai/controls.ts`: `generate()/preview()/send()/discard()` produce manual unsaved drafts. Separately, `openActivity()`, `tick()`, `simulate()` and `runActivityBatch()` are supposed to automatically generate and commit scheduled AI posts. Review interactions: today `tick()` can be paused by a manual `draft` and respects visit attempt budget; simplify appropriately after removing normal manual generation.
- `src/ai/activity.ts`: individual `nextDue` and seeded activity/quiet-time decisions; default `maxPosts=4` but `consent=false` until explicit model authorization. `src/main.ts` calls activity on startup/reconnect/visibility and once per visible minute. Verify rather than assume these triggers actually produce due posts after consent.
- `src/storage/repository.ts`: atomic `commitAiRun`, saved `ai-activity`, authorization, profiles, cross-tab reset/restore safety. `src/ai/activity-runner.ts` consumes plans. `src/storage/community.ts` and `data/pcvan/fictional-community.json`: thirty bundled seed posts must remain intact and later serve as eligible reply/memory context.
- Existing user intent: “Why must a user explicitly run GENERATE? That is wrong; except for initial model download consent, residents should just live and talk themselves.” **Do not interpret this as permission for an unprompted huge model download.**
- Contribution workflow: [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/blob/main/AGENTS.md), [Issue template](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/blob/main/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/issue.md), [development flow](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/blob/main/docs/development-flow.md). Issue/PR/docs in English; product copy in Japanese.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Ordinary Settings/Help no longer contains a manual `GENERATE` → `PREVIEW` → `SEND` workflow or prompts visitors to choose which AI persona posts where. Resident occupation/behavior editors, global activity/pause settings and AI model selection remain usable from the modern Settings dialog. If retained, developer diagnostics are strictly opt-in and do not masquerade as PC-VAN participation.
- [ ] After a user explicitly authorizes and successfully loads a WebGPU local model, **without opening Settings again or issuing any manual AI-generation command**, due resident opportunities produce validated, automatically saved posts/replies. From the user's viewpoint AI content simply appears on a later `LIST`/forum visit. Correctly distinguish scheduling silence vs errors and model not ready in on-demand app diagnostics.
- [ ] While an eligible page stays visibly open, due work is processed automatically on its existing timer/visibility triggers; the terminal remains responsive. If a human posts, an interested resident may later reply at *that resident's* scheduled opportunity, not through an immediate chatbot handler. AI residents can converse with one another using proper same-forum reply references.
- [ ] After closing and reopening the browser, auto activity reconstructs a bounded subset of plausible elapsed work chronologically with no user prompt except an actual missing/revoked model permission. No actual background inference is claimed. Initial seed posts remain accessible independent of the model.
- [ ] Settings transparently conveys whether auto activity is **enabled, paused, waiting on initial model authorization, loading, waiting for a due time, processing, or blocked/failed**, without introducing “AI住人がいます!” signage in the normal terminal. Failures (WebGPU unavailable, cache/weights missing, model load/validation failure, locks unavailable, quota) do not turn into a requirement to manually author/approve posts or break human posting.
- [ ] Preserve current opt-in consent for heavyweight initial downloads; no model download on mere page visit or Settings open. Later loads may reuse an approved model per current consent rules. Pausing/STOP cancels work, per-resident pause is respected, switching models requires renewed consent and pending work is not silently lost or double-committed.
- [ ] Automatic generations use existing transactional numbered posts, stable AI IDs and explicit `origin`/simulation timestamps; maintain 10 character profiles, 30 seeded messages, per-board reply constraints, readable handle rendering, IndexedDB persistence, JSON backup/import/reset compatibility and cross-tab idempotency.
- [ ] Add deterministic mock-LLM, fake-clock browser/E2E tests that **never touch the manual generation API**: new profile with bundled posts → explicit model consent → scheduled posts while page stays open → human `WRITE` or `REPLY` → delayed automated resident response → AI-to-AI response → close/reopen and bounded catch-up → LIST/READ results. Include quiet periods, default on/off, unsupported GPU, model failure, model change, per-profile pause and two tabs; verify no manual-generation controls appear in standard UI.
- [ ] Update README and `docs/local-ai.md` to explain the ordinary automatic behavior, first-time consent, noninstant/quiet-period scheduling, failure diagnostics and the fact that humans **never need to press GENERATE or SAVE for AI residents**. Update all UI help strings and tests to reflect the actual supported paths; run `npm test` / `npm run build` and record actual results.

## Optional validation

On compatible desktop WebGPU hardware, enable the model once and leave the site open/revisit after enough scheduled time to observe natural conversation progression without manual intervention. Review character consistency and perceived pacing; this real-GPU subjective check is useful but not a pre-merge gate.

## Required post-merge verification

None required. Scheduler behavior can be tested in a local production build with mocked WebLLM, fake time, IndexedDB and browser interaction checks; hosted deployment is handled separately.
